description:
Every supported installation, deployment, MCP, compatibility, upgrade, and version-policy workflow has one maintained adopter-facing home.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `INSTALL.md` owns installing the published native archive and verifying its checksum, plus the contributor build-from-checkout path; `docs/how-to/deployment.md` owns the one-image `/repo` deployment including building that image locally; a canonical MCP guide owns installing the released tarball and starting it from a client; and the release-policy reference owns version, compatibility, upgrade, artifact, and MSRV procedures.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every command, artifact name, mount path, health URL, runtime prerequisite, and version policy stated in those homes is exercised by automation or derived from a maintained manifest or workflow source.
- [hard] REQ-03: The canonical pages distinguish the published artifacts from contributor source-checkout workflows, and no instruction depends on an artifact the release does not publish.
- [hard] REQ-04: Link, command-snippet, and support-matrix checks fail when a canonical path is missing, stale, or duplicated.
- [hard] REQ-05: The pages state that v1.0 publishes one GitHub release and no package-registry or container-registry version, so an adopter can tell which distribution paths are supported without inferring it.

## Notes

Blast radius: `INSTALL.md`, `docs/how-to/deployment.md`, the canonical MCP integration page (created if absent), one release-policy reference, navigation, and documentation checks; historical and unrelated conceptual documents are unchanged.
title: Establish canonical installation, deployment, MCP, source, and release references
